title: On the quantum communication complexity of total functions
abstract: We present a total function with a polylogarithmic two-message quantum protocol, whereas every randomised protocol, even with arbitrarily many rounds, requires polynomial communication.
summary: This paper constructs a specific total Boolean function, Cheat-Shapen, to demonstrate a separation between quantum and classical communication complexity. It achieves a polylogarithmic quantum communication protocol while requiring a super-polynomial randomized protocol. This highlights the computational power of quantum communication protocols for certain tasks.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct a total Boolean function that demonstrates a significant separation between its quantum communication complexity and its classical randomized communication complexity.
main_result: The authors present a function, Cheat-Shapen, with a polylogarithmic two-message quantum communication protocol, while its randomized communication complexity is shown to be super-polynomial in the input size.
method: The construction combines three elements: the shifted approximate equality problem (Shape), a communication cheat-sheet construction, and a fully linear PCP derived from multiplication gates.
model_or_system: The analysis is based on the communication complexity of a specific total Boolean function, Cheat-Shapen, which is defined using multiple instances of the Shape problem.
key_observables: Quantum communication complexity ($	ext{Q}_{1/3}(	ext{Cheat-Shapen}) \in O(\log^3 n \log \log n)$) and randomized communication complexity ($	ext{R}_{1/3}(	ext{Cheat-Shapen}) \in \Omega( rac{N_n}{6} \sqrt{n} \log^{7/3} N_n)$).
important_parameters: The input size parameters $n$ and $k$, and the total input size $N_n = 2nk + M(1 + \ell_n)$.
main_assumptions: The quantum protocol relies on an established one-way consequence for the Shape problem, and the PCP construction requires viewing $1 - D_{n,k}$ as an arithmetic circuit over a characteristic-two field.
paper_structure: The paper proves Theorem 1 by combining the derived quantum protocol bound (Equation 12) with the established classical lower bound (Equations 15 and 17).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, information-theoretic example of quantum advantage in communication complexity, which is a fundamental area of quantum information theory.
